newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa still in intensive care but stable.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa still in intensive care but stable.

text.p: Mother Teresa was conscious and in a stable condition in intensive care on Saturday after suffering heart trouble, doctors said.
The 86-year-old Roman Catholic missionary was rushed to Calcutta's Woodlands Nursing Home early on Friday, the third time since August that she had been taken to the hospital for emergency care.
A doctor said on Saturday that Mother Teresa's heart continued to beat irregularly but she was not in critical condition and was "comfortable".
The legendary nun, who was fitted with a heart pacemaker in 1989, was initially put on a respirator to help her breathe but was later taken off the machine, doctors said.
"Her recovery is satisfactory and she has improved a lot," Dr Asim Bardhan, her cardiologist, told reporters on Friday night.
Since she was fitted with the pacemaker in 1989, Mother Teresa has spent time in hospital for heart disease, bacterial pneumonia, broken ribs, malaria, and lung problems.
She spent nearly three weeks at Woodlands Nursing Home in late August and early September for heart trouble, malaria and pneumonia.

Two weeks after returning to her Calcutta-based order, she fell off a chair and hit her head. A brain scan revealed a blood clot in her brain but it disappeared and she was later released from hospital.
Last Saturday, Mother Teresa received honorary American citizenship, one of only five people in U.S. history, in a ceremony led by U.S. Ambassador to India Frank Wisner.
Diminutive and bowed, her head often shrouded in a sari, Mother Teresa has became a symbol of commitment to the destitute and is considered a living saint to her multitude of followers.
She began her life's work in the slums of Calcutta, India's most densely populated city, in 1949 and has won worldwide admiration for her devotion to the poor.
